import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_59/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_59/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_59/training_2.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # movie_id, title, genres
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # user_id, gender, age, occupation, zip
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # user_id, movie_id, rating, timestamp

# First join: df2 with df1 on user_id
df_join1 = pd.merge(df2, df1, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Second join: result with df0 on movie_id
df_final = pd.merge(df_join1, df0, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = [
    'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp',
    'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip',
    'title', 'genres'
]
df_final = df_final[target_columns]

# Ensure data types match target schema
df_final = df_final.astype({
    'user_id': 'int64',
    'movie_id': 'int64',
    'rating': 'int64',
    'timestamp': 'int64',
    'gender': 'string',
    'age': 'int64',
    'occupation': 'int64',
    'zip': 'string',
    'title': 'string',
    'genres': 'string'
})

# Write the final dataframe to the specified path without the index
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_59/target_multisource.csv"
df_final.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_59/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_59/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_59/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source2_59_2 and Source2_59_1 on user_id
df = pd.merge(source2, source1, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source2_59_0 on movie_id
df = pd.merge(df, source0, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Group by all columns (no aggregation needed since no duplicates expected)
# This ensures no duplicate rows and matches target schema exactly
df = df.groupby(
    ["user_id", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp", "gender", "age", "occupation", "zip", "title", "genres"],
    as_index=False
).size()  # size() just to trigger groupby, but we don't need the count

# Drop the size column created by size()
df = df.drop(columns=["size"])

# Write the final output to the target file
df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_59/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
